questions.title: p for infinitely many solutions
questions.text: The value of 'p' for which the equations px + 3y = p − 3, 12x + py = p has infinitely many solutions is:
steps: ① Infinitely many ⟹ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂
questions.remember:
Unique: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂
Infinite: all three equal
None: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂
questions.trap: Stopping at p² = 36 and choosing ±6. Check the third ratio too!
questions.tryit: For what k does kx + 2y = 5, 3x + y = 1 have a unique solution?

questions.title: Consistent or inconsistent?
questions.text: The pair of linear equations 3x/2 + 5y/3 = 7 and 9x + 10y = 14 is:
steps: ④ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ ⟹ parallel lines
questions.remember: Consistent = at least one solution. Parallel lines = inconsistent.
questions.trap: Comparing ratios before clearing the fractions.
questions.tryans: Yes: coincident lines, infinitely many solutions

questions.title: Tarun's other line
questions.text:
Tarun correctly solved a pair of linear equations and found their only point of intersection as (5, −1). One of the lines was x − y = 6. Which could have been the other line?
I: 3x − 3y = 18     II: 2x − 3y = 13     III: 2x − 3y = 16
steps: ① Two tests: passes through (5, −1) AND crosses x − y = 6 only once
② I: 15 + 3 = 18 ✓ … but ÷ 3 gives x − y = 6: the SAME line ✗
questions.remember: 'Only point of intersection' ⟹ the lines must cross exactly once.
questions.trap: Choosing I because (5, −1) fits it. It's the same line, so infinitely many points!
questions.tryit: Write another line through (5, −1) that meets x − y = 6 only once.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: p = 1
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The pair of linear equations px + 3y + 59 = 0 and 2x + 6y + 118 = 0 will have infinitely many solutions if p = 1.
Reason (R): If the pair of linear equations px + 3y + 19 = 0 and 2x + 6y + 157 = 0 has a unique solution, then p ≠ 1.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ② So p/2 = 1/2 ⟹ p = 1  ✓ A true
③ R: unique ⟹ p/2 ≠ 3/6 ⟹ p ≠ 1  ✓ R true
④ R is about a DIFFERENT pair (the unique case)
questions.remember: Two true statements ≠ option (a). Ask: does R explain A?
questions.trap: Picking (a) because both use p = 1. R is about a different pair of equations.
questions.tryit: For what p do px + 3y = 5, 2x + 6y = 7 have no solution?

questions.title: Solve 7x − 2y = 5, 8x + 7y = 15
questions.text: Solve the following system of linear equations 7x − 2y = 5 and 8x + 7y = 15 and verify your answer.
questions.remember: Make one variable's coefficients opposite, then add.
questions.trap: Skipping 'verify' when the question asks for it. That's a lost mark.

questions.title: The add–subtract trick: 37x + 63y
questions.text: Solve the following system of equations algebraically: 37x + 63y = 137, 63x + 37y = 163
steps: ① Coefficients swap places ⟹ add, then subtract!
④ Add these: 2x = 4 ⟹ x = 2,  then y = 1
questions.remember: Swapped coefficients? Add the equations, then subtract them.
questions.trap: Multiplying by 37 and 63. It works, but it's slow and error-prone.

questions.title: Ages: Rashmi and Nazma
questions.text: Three years ago, Rashmi was thrice as old as Nazma. Ten years later, Rashmi will be twice as old as Nazma. How old are Rashmi and Nazma now?
steps: ① Let Rashmi = x, Nazma = y (ages NOW)
④ Subtract ②'s equation from ③'s: y = 16
questions.remember: Let the ages NOW be x and y. Shift BOTH ages by the same years.
questions.trap: Writing x − 3 = 3y (forgetting Nazma was also 3 years younger).
questions.tryit: Five years ago, A was thrice B. Ten years later, A will be twice B. Present ages?

questions.title: Incomes 9 : 7, expenditures 4 : 3
questions.text: The monthly incomes of two persons are in the ratio 9 : 7 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 4 : 3. If each saved ₹5,000, express the situation algebraically as a system of linear equations and hence find their respective monthly incomes.
questions.remember: A ratio a : b becomes ax and bx. Savings = income − expenditure.
questions.trap: Giving x = 5000 as the answer. The question asks for the INCOMES: 9x and 7x.
questions.tryit: Incomes 3 : 2, expenditures 5 : 3, each saves ₹2,000. Find the incomes.

questions.title: Rectangle: length and breadth (5 marks)
questions.text: If the length of a rectangle is reduced by 5 cm and its breadth is increased by 2 cm, then the area of the rectangle is reduced by 80 cm². However, if we increase the length by 10 cm and decrease the breadth by 5 cm, its area is increased by 50 cm². Find the length and breadth of the rectangle.
steps: ① Length x, breadth y, area xy
questions.remember: Area word problems: expand, and the xy term cancels, leaving a linear equation.
questions.tryit: A rectangle's length is 4 cm more than its breadth; perimeter 48 cm. Find its sides.

questions.title: Case study: the sanitizer business
questions.text:
A student entrepreneur sells sanitizer in small (₹10) and large (₹15) bottles. In June, 1000 bottles were sold for ₹12,750. In July, each price went up by ₹2, and 2500 bottles were sold for ₹34,250.
(i) Equation for June's sale.  (ii) Equation for July's sale.  (iii) How many bottles of each type were sold in June? [OR: in July?]
steps: ① Small bottles = x, large bottles = y
⑥ July the same way: x = 1650,  y = 850
∴ June 450 small, 550 large · July 1650 small, 850 large
questions.ans: June 450 small, 550 large · July 1650 small, 850 large
questions.remember: Case studies: name the variables first, then write one equation per sentence.
questions.trap: Using the old prices (₹10, ₹15) for July. Prices went up by ₹2.
